messages:
maria: FYI I hit a puzzling CI failure after bumping the eviction window. Two different nodes reported resident=true for prefix/tenantX/foo with different slot ids and we served stale reads until a demote finally reconciled.

maria: tail of the logs (condensed):
```
[2026-02-11T02:14:01Z] node-4: mark resident tenantX/foo slot=3
[2026-02-11T02:14:02Z] node-7: mark resident tenantX/foo slot=11
[2026-02-11T02:14:10Z] demote node-4 -> ack delayed
[2026-02-11T02:14:12Z] read tenantX/foo -> returned node-4 cached value (stale)
```

ajay: sounds like demote ack lost or delayed and node-4 kept believing it owned the prefix. Did you repro with handoff overlap? was this under churn?

maria: yes heavy handoff + eviction churn. repro script attached to the ticket I filed.

lin: there are a couple of angles here: (A) strengthen demote path to revoke outstanding resident marks; (B) make claim handshake require a short reservation nonce so the old owner can't silently re-assert; (C) do a reader-side validation that checks a small lease tag before trusting cache.

kevin: I prototyped (B) a few months ago (reservation cookie). Idea: claim RPC returns a reservation nonce; claim completes only once nonce is in metadata and is > previous; old owner must include its last-seen nonce when trying to re-mark and will be rejected if mismatch. Nonce garbage collects after short TTL.

lin: pros/cons: cookie is cheap and avoids bumping general epoch counters. downside: more protocol state and TTL tuning. Also requires us to surface nonce in telemetry so we can debug replays.

ajay: (C) reader-side validation seems promising: cheap extra check on misses/hits where the read path validates owner_tombstone/nonce before using cached result. Could mitigate stale reads during windows without changing claim semantics.

maria: we did a quick experiment in staging where reads did a single metadata read-if-stale check and dropped stale cache. Tail latency went up slightly but still acceptable for our SLOs.

kevin: another idea: adopt a two-phase resident set update: mark-resident-intent -> consensus write -> mark-resident-commit. Intent has short TTL and is only used to prevent concurrent claims. Commit flips resident bit. It's heavier but makes the race explicit.

lin: that ends up being similar to epoch CAS but modeled as two writes. If we can atomic CAS epoch + owner it's simpler for correctness proofs. Cookie or intent moves complexity to RPC semantics though.

maria: operation requirements: must be compatible with Dedicated/Private where metadata store sometimes has different latency/consistency. Any proposal must be tolerant to slow metadata stores and safely degrade.

ajay: for Private, we can't rely on a single global TTL; maybe prefer reader-validation there, because control plane ops are slower. For Hosted we can enable nonce/intent flow with tighter TTLs.

kevin: mechanics for reservation cookie:
- claim RPC: write metadata.reservation = {nonce, claimer_id, expires_at}
- claim ack: only after metadata.owner updated to claimer and reservation nonce still matches
- demote: remove reservation or increment tombstone
- re-mark by old owner will include last_known_nonce and get explicit reject if mismatch

kevin: we need a small guard to avoid denial-of-service where a noisy claimer floods reservations. rate-limit reservations per-tenant-per-shard.

lin: testing plan suggestions:
- deterministic sim with interleaved demote/claim/retry/replay
- chaos test that drops demote acks and replays pre-demote writes
- reader-side canary on 5% of reads that validate metadata and log mismatches

maria: metrics to add: reservation.rejections, reservation.ttl_expiry_count, reader.stale_hit_rejects, double_resident_gauge. ops-bot can create dash.

ops-bot: created dash tile 'evict-reservation: reservation.rejections' (user=ops-bot, id=EVICT-529)

ajay: rollout plan I'd propose:
1) lightweight reader-side validation globally (fail open but emit metric)
2) enable reservation cookie for hosted via feature flag on 20% of shards
3) run chaos for 4h, monitor reservation.rejections and double_resident_gauge
4) if stable, flip flag to 100% hosted, leave Private on reader-validation for now

maria: implementation owner? @kevin volunteer? I'll own the sim harness and run the repro during canary.

kevin: will take reservation proto + unit tests. I'll also add telemetry fields to spans with nonce and reservation state.

lin: compatibility note: make reservation optional. metadata readers treat missing reservation as legacy flow. Add rollout toggles in node agent.

maria: ok creating GH#5234 with repro and proposed sim. linking PRs once ready. thanks all.

kevin: one more ops note: set reservation TTL to something like 5s by default and tune during canary. too short -> rej retries; too long -> blocked claims.

maria: final: attaching repro script to GH#5234. last_message: I'll kick off canary once kevin has the PR.
